distinguishing_features: Adds physical helical strakes to the stationary shroud to disrupt coherent vortex shedding, a hardware geometry change none of the prior art employs.
Attacks flow-induced dynamic excitation at its source rather than retuning an operating schedule (Art 1) or inferring failure from signals/thermodynamic proxies (Arts 2, 3).
Targets suppression of fluid-structure resonance amplification affecting weld fatigue, a physical-structure remedy absent from the monitoring/procedure prior art.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce resonant structural response of a rotating centrifuge bowl excited by fluid-flow dynamics so that weld fatigue cracking at the operating speed is prevented.
parsed.viable_reason: The physics is implausible as written: centrifuge processing flow is far below the 50 m/s peripheral-scale velocity assumed, the stationary-shroud gap does not shed coherent vortices at resonance-relevant frequencies, and strakes on a stationary shroud cannot practically alter the bowl's synchronous imbalance-driven resonance or be validated by the stated 500 Hz/3-5x figures.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying vortex-shedding suppression by adding helical strakes to coherent-flow-excited structures is a known offshore/marine mitigation technique, but transferring it here is not a routine parameter tweak of any of the cited prior art, so the distinguishing mechanism itself is not obvious from those references.
